tickets.name: Build IconNode — custom node with icon + label + acquired toggle
Build NodePalette — side panel to drag items from
Build edge drawing — directed connections between nodes
Build Toolbar — mode switcher (select / connect / pan)
Body assertions: assert.<path> on api nodes
tickets.description:
Problem: expect only checks the response STATUS. A flow that gets 200 back
with the wrong number in the body still scores green — FML confirms the API
responded, not that it said the right thing. Raised by a Claude session
working on stablishMind, testing an income calc (link bank -> sync ->
income): "the one thing to build first is body assertions ... without that,
FML tests are smoke tests not correctness tests." Confirmed against the
codebase 2026-10-09 — real gap, right priority call.

What to build: a new `assert.<name>: <expr>` dotted key on `api` nodes, same
shape as `capture.<var>` (repeatable, suffix is just a label for error
messages — not a variable name, nothing stores it). Reuses readPath() from
run.ts to pull the value out of the response, the same path syntax
capture already uses ($.data.income_rate, status, header.<Name>).

Comparison grammar for <expr>:
  - bare value           exact match after type coercion (assert.status: active)
  - ~N                   numeric, within tolerance of N (need to pick: relative
                          1% default, or require an explicit range like
                          ~11900+-50 -- decide before implementing, affects
                          the grammar)
  - >= <= > < !=          numeric comparison
  - anything else         treated as exact string match

Needs: readPath() currently can't resolve `.length` on an array (pathTokens
walks object keys / numeric indices only) -- `assert.sources.length: >= 2`
from the motivating example needs this. Add array .length as a special-cased
terminal token in readPath, not a general feature.

Failure semantics: match `expect`'s philosophy exactly -- an assert failure
marks the step failed (red) but does NOT stop the walk by itself; it follows
the drawn edge same as a failed status expect does today (stopOnFailure still
the fail-fast override). Captures run first, then expect, then asserts --
order matters because an assert can reference a value this same node just
captured.

Ripple (per CLAUDE.md -- language changes touch all of these):
  - src/fml/run.ts: buildRequest already reads node.data generically, this is
    new logic in runNode -- parse the comparison grammar, evaluate, fold into
    StepResult alongside captures/expect. readPath gets .length support.
  - src/fml/nodeTypes.ts: add "assert" to EXEC_KEY_PREFIXES so it's not
    flagged as an unknown key (same as header./query./capture.).
  - src/fml/lint.ts: malformed assert expression (bad operator, empty path)
    gets flagged the same way an empty capture.x: path is today.
  - HOW-TO.md: new section under the `api` keys reference, same treatment as
    the "Multiple hosts in one file" section.
  - examples/: extend one example (or add a new one) that fails on purpose
    via assert so the behavior is demonstrated, not just described.
  - Tests: run.test.ts (grammar parsing, .length on an array, pass/fail/stop
    semantics), lint.test.ts (malformed assert flagged).

Explicitly NOT in scope for this ticket (separate follow-ups, see
lore/ideas/flow-execution.md):
  - Conditional ROUTING on a captured/asserted value (branching on
    {income_rate} > 10000 instead of status) -- valuable but a different
    problem; this ticket is about scoring a step, not choosing an edge.
  - Test-data seeding / a `setup` node type -- FML has no backend-state
    concept today by design; probably stays Django's job (dedicated test
    fixtures/accounts) rather than something FML owns. Needs its own
    decision, not bundled in here.

Open question before starting: the tolerance syntax for ~N (relative %
default vs. requiring an explicit range) -- pick one before writing the
parser, it's the one part of the grammar without an obvious right answer.
